answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network applies topological cut verifications across multi-agent interaction graphs alongside cross-auditing. If a node cluster attempts collusion, an ember of audit queries reveals disconnected dense subgraphs. When fraud is proven, stake slashing triggers, wiping deposits like shale crumbling under stress. Because passing topological cuts requires authentic edge expansion, the attacker face superlinear costs; forging identities vanishes like a zephyr against the collective proof.
